answer: A vault of identities stays honest when each one must periodically solve a fresh puzzle tied to its own key, like a walnut that only cracks with its own shell: work done for one identity cannot be replayed for another. The twist is funding-aware difficulty: identities funded from the same source face puzzles that grow steeply harder with each additional identity, so a dune of cheap copies quickly becomes a mountain of computation. An attacker must therefore pay real, non-reusable compute per fake, while a single honest agent faces only a trivial puzzle.
